description: What a normal hotel engagement looks like. A guest's agent compares an offer's derived terms against these and flags only the deviations; severity is a hint, and escalation is the agent's decision.

norms.title: Time to dispute after checkout
norms.why: This is how long you have to answer a deposit claim or report a problem. If it's short, your silence costs you before you even notice: an unanswered claim stands.

norms.title: Time to dispute a problem on arrival
norms.why: If there's no room or the wrong room, this is how long you have to raise it. Too short, and the no-show payout to the hotel can fire first.

norms.title: How long the hotel has to confirm
norms.why: Until the hotel confirms, your money is tied up with no booking. A long wait leaves you unable to book elsewhere.

norms.title: How long the arbiter has to rule
norms.why: While a dispute is open, the money is frozen. A long ruling deadline means a long wait for your refund.

norms.title: How long the hotel has to claim against your deposit
norms.why: Your deposit is held until this passes. A long claim window keeps it locked longer.

norms.title: Deposit size
norms.why: A deposit above half the room price is unusual. It's held for the whole stay and can be claimed against.

norms.title: Service fee
norms.why: Engagement fees are normally at most 1% of what the hotel receives.

norms.title: Arbiter is accredited
norms.why: The arbiter can rule with the hotel alone to pay the hotel. It must be an accredited, independent provider, not someone the hotel simply named.

norms.title: Backup arbiter is accredited
norms.why: The backup rules when the arbiter goes silent. It must be an accredited, independent provider too.

norms.title: Backup arbiter isn't the hotel's pick
norms.why: If the hotel also chose the backup, a stalled or biased arbiter leaves you with another arbiter the hotel picked.

norms.title: Hotel can't take the money alone
norms.why: The hotel should never be able to move the money without you, an arbiter, or the policy co-signer.

norms.title: The policy can't be skipped
norms.why: Even you and the hotel together shouldn't be able to move the money without the policy co-signer (or an arbiter), so the agreed rules always apply.
